6/7 - Weekly post about the funny books

3 from Image and 1 from Zenescope. No love for the others this week.

Cannibal #6

Written by Brian Buccellato and Jennifer Young. Art and Cover by Matias Bergara. Grady and Louise must deal with the ramifications of Danny's escape from prison as Cash comes to grips with Jolene's fate. Cover price $3.99.

Reborn #6

Written by Mark Millar. Art by Greg Capullo & Various. Cover by Greg Capullo. MINI-SERIES FINALE! The big finale of the smash-hit MILLAR-CAPULLO series REBORN is here. The action-packed climax sees Bonnie taking revenge on past enemies and finding her husband Harry, with Big Tom and Roy-Boy by her side. Cover price $5.99.

Youngblood #2

Written by Chad Bowers. Art and Cover by Jim Towe. 'YOUNGBLOOD REBORN,' Part Two The 'Blood is back, baby! But for how long? Shaft arrives in Baltimore with a warning for the team of rookie heroes calling themselves 'Youngblood,' but will it fall on deaf ears? Meanwhile, President Die Hard meets with the architects of the popular Help! app and struggles with just how far he's willing to go to protect the country. All this, plus Badrock keeping secrets? Seriously, Badrock…already? What the hell, dude, it's only the second issue? Cover price $3.99.

Day of the Dead #5

Written by Dawn P. Marquez. Art and Cover by Allan Otero. The Order of Tarot's plan comes to fruition, transforming Mary into her new persona…the powerful and dark Mystere. The Order's plan is for her to be the new Queen of Pentacles and only Talisman can stop them. Unfortunately Judgment has a different idea…and that's for him to be the King of Pentacles at Mary's side, carrying out Tarot's plan to rule the world. Cover price $3.99.

• Bane Conquest #2, Batman #24, Nightwing #22: It's awesome to see Chuck Dixon writing for DC again.

  • Transformers: Lost Light #6: The conclusion to the first storyline of the new as Megatron, Rodimus, and the crew have to decide whether they can destroy their only way back to their universe in order to save the universe they're in from the Functionists.

  • Amazing Spider-man #28, Daredevil #21, Spider-man/Deadpool #18

On a side note, I've started to subscribe to the two main Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles series from IDW (TMNT and Universe) which moves IDW above Marvel and DC for most titles subscribed to (though I still get more DC issues per month because of twice a month issues). And it drops down Marvel into my least titles subscribed to (where I subscribe to at least two since technically I get Savage Dragon from Image and Usagi Yojimbo from Dark Horse). Marvel can keep trying to get me to buy a bazillion Spider-man titles a month, but it just isn't going to work.

How do the two TMNT books compare to each other? I was buying the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles when it was first coming out, and was quite impressed by it. The other day I saw what issue they were up to and couldn't believe how far behind I became. I probably wont try to catch up unless I get an itch to pick up some trades. Just interested in how Universe stacked up against it.

I've only read a few issues of Universe because I still have a few gaps in the main series and as such I haven't gone beyond #29 yet, but so far they've been solid. It reminds me a bit of All-Star Batman where there's a main story which is separate, but references what's going on in the other title(s) and a back-up story which is completely self-contained.
